Build a Hypergraph from Group Memberships

Source: R/bipartite_groups.R
bipartite_groups.Rd

bipartite_groups() builds a hypergraph from long-format membership data, in which each row records that a player took part in a group (a session, team, project, transaction or any other group context), and returns a net_hypergraph. Each distinct group becomes one hyperedge spanning the players that appeared in it. The incidence matrix of players by groups is 0/1, or holds summed weights when weight is given.

Usage

bipartite_groups(data, player, group, weight = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per membership (a player in a group), holding the player, group and, when used, weight columns. Rows with a missing value in any of these columns are dropped without a message; when no row is left, an error is raised.

player

The name of the column whose values become the nodes (players, participants, actors). Values are read as character and the nodes are sorted. A name that is not a single column of data raises an error, as for group and weight.

group

The name of the column whose values become the hyperedges (groups, sessions, teams). Values are read as character, and the hyperedges follow their sorted order (as text, so "10" comes before "2").

weight

The name of a numeric column summed per player and group to give a weighted incidence matrix. With the default NULL, the matrix is 0/1, and a player listed more than once in a group counts once. With weights, a player belongs to a group when the summed weight is positive; a group with no such member is dropped, and a player left without a group stays a node.

Value

A net_hypergraph, the class build_hypergraph() returns. Print it for the numbers of nodes and hyperedges and the hyperedge sizes; summary() prints the counts with the mean and largest hyperedge size, and returns a data frame of node degrees (node, and degree, the number of hyperedges a player belongs to). hypergraph_measures(), hypergraph_centrality(), hypergraph_laplacian() and hypergraph_cluster() read it. The fields:

hyperedges

An unnamed list with one vector per hyperedge, in the sorted order of the groups: the indices of its players in nodes, sorted and named by player.

incidence

The players-by-groups matrix, one column per hyperedge, with player and group names as dimnames: integer 0/1, or the summed weights (a player whose sum is zero or negative keeps that sum here but is not a member of the hyperedge).

nodes

The player names, sorted.

n_nodes, n_hyperedges

The numbers of players and of hyperedges (after dropping empty groups).

size_distribution

A named integer vector with the number of hyperedges of each size (size_1, size_2, ...).

params

A list with source = "bipartite_groups", the column names given as player, group and weight, and n_observations, the number of rows used.

Details

The bipartite representation preserves the full group structure without projecting to a pairwise network. A group of three players A, B, C produces a single 3-hyperedge containing all three, not three pairwise edges AB, AC, BC. This avoids information loss when group interactions are the primary unit of analysis (Perc et al. 2013).

Unlike build_hypergraph() (which derives hyperedges from a network's clique structure), bipartite_groups() takes group memberships directly. The two functions are complementary:

  • bipartite_groups() - when group membership is observed (sessions, transactions, co-authorships).

  • build_hypergraph() - when only pairwise interactions are observed and group structure must be inferred from cliques (triangles by default).

Note

(experimental) Validated against a hand-computed table() incidence reference only; no independent R package exposes the long-format-to-binary-incidence primitive, because the operation is definitionally table(). The code path is a direct one-to-one restatement of its definition.

References

Perc, M., Gomez-Gardenes, J., Szolnoki, A., Floria, L. M., & Moreno, Y. (2013). Evolutionary dynamics of group interactions on structured populations: a review. Journal of the Royal Society Interface 10(80), 20120997. doi:10.1098/rsif.2012.0997

See also

build_hypergraph() for the clique-based constructor.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  player = c("Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Alice", "Bob",
             "Dave", "Carol", "Dave", "Eve"),
  session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2",
              "S3", "S3", "S3", "S3")
)
hg <- bipartite_groups(df, player = "player", group = "session")
print(hg)
#> Hypergraph: 5 nodes, 3 hyperedges
#> Size distribution:
#>   size_2   : 1
#>   size_3   : 2
summary(hg)
#> Hypergraph summary
#>   Nodes:         5
#>   Hyperedges:    3
#>   Mean size:     2.67
#>   Max size:      3
#>    node degree
#> 1 Alice      2
#> 2   Bob      2
#> 3 Carol      2
#> 4  Dave      1
#> 5   Eve      1
